question.worked_solution:
The "square of a sum" formula states that

$$
{x}^{2}+2xy+{y}^{2}=(x+y)^{2}.
$$

We will use this formula to factor the given trinomial. Our trinomial is

$$
9{b}^{2}+24b+16.
$$

First, we write both the quadratic term and the constant term as perfect squares:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3b)^{2}+24b+(4)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we factor a $2$ out of the linear term:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3b)^{2}+2(12b)+(4)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we write the middle parentheses $(12b)$ as a product of $3b$ and $4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(3b)^{2}+2(3b\cdot 4)+(4)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we factor the trinomial using the square of a sum formula with $x=3b$ and $y=4.$ This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}(3b+4)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
